title: Freedom Isn't a Day. It's a Debt.
description: Reframes freedom not as a single achieved moment, but as an ongoing debt society keeps asking you to repay.

title: The Currency Problem: Why India Keeps Having Children Until It Gets a Son
description: Examines how families treat sons as an economic asset and daughters as a debt, and what that does to the children caught in between.

title: The Psychology of Being Compared to the Perfect Child
description: On the psychological cost of growing up measured against an idealized sibling or standard that was never really achievable.

title: The Entire Self-Help Industry Is Built on One Lie — And You Already Know What It Is
description: A critique of the self-help industry's core premise, and what it conveniently leaves out.

title: Consortivulnus: I Made a Word for a Wound That Had No Name
description: The original essay introducing Consortivulnus — a term for the specific harm of being hurt by someone who shares your own condition.

title: The Witness Problem
description: On perception and testimony — what it means to witness something, and why that's less reliable than it feels.

title: Can You Love Life and Still Believe It Has No Inherent Meaning??
description: Asks whether loving life requires believing it has inherent meaning, or whether the two can coexist without contradiction.

title: 5 Problems with Modern Feminism and Solutions
description: A critical look at five specific shortcomings in how modern feminism is practiced, with a proposed fix for each.

title: How Religious Creation Myths Became the Blueprint for the Systemic Oppression of Women
description: Traces how religious creation narratives set the template later used to justify the systemic oppression of women.

title: The Goodness of the Godless
description: Asks whether morality requires God, contrasting goodness done out of fear or reward with goodness done because another person matters.

title: Meaning Is Built, Not Found
description: Argues that meaning in life isn't something waiting to be discovered, but something constructed.
